resources.string: Each turn you fire one shell. Set the angle and power with the sliders, or drag back from your tank like a slingshot, then press Fire.
The wind changes every turn. The arrow and number show which way it pushes and how hard. The dotted line previews the first moments of your shot, wind included.
A shell digs a crater and hurts every tank near it, most of all on a direct hit. Craters change the ground: you can bury a tank or leave it exposed.
Big shells dig wide and hit hard; bouncers hop over hills before they explode. Each tank carries only a few, so save them for the right moment.
Tap Hint for a suggested shot, or Undo to take your last shot back. The last tank standing wins.
Artillery duels, where players adjust angle and power to lob shells over hills, date back to mainframe programs of the early 1960s and became a PC classic in the early 1990s.
Tap a target to shoot it. Ducks score 10 (25 when small), rings score by zone up to 50, and a gold star scores 50 and refills your magazine.
Never shoot the spiky decoy: it costs 30 points and breaks your combo. Look for the cross on it.
Your magazine holds six shots and then reloads. Shots fired while it reloads are wasted, so pick your targets. You can also reload early.
Hit targets in a row to build a combo up to times four. A miss or a decoy breaks it. Every player gets the same range, so it is all skill.
Cannot tap fast? Choose Relaxed pace: slower, larger targets, more time and a quicker reload. A Shoot nearest target button helps too.
Shooting galleries were fairground staples by the late 1800s, and the tin ducks gliding along a rail are still the picture most people have of one.
